value: Study population: 15 Yanomami from Brazil; 8 Yanomami from Venezuela; 24 Matses; 12 Tunapuco; 44 United States urban individuals
Sequencing method: Shotgun metagenomic analysis using HiSeq 2500, ~14 million reads per sample average
Taxonomic profiling: Kraken with NCBI bacterial/archaeal genomes database
Functional profiling: SUPER-FOCUS based on SEED database gene families
Statistical methods: Kruskal-Wallis test, LDA (LEfSe), PERMANOVA, Wilcoxon test
Yanomami lifestyle: semi-nomadic hunter-gatherers with swidden horticulture, diet low in fat and salt, high in fruits and fiber
Ethics approval: Oswaldo Cruz Foundation Ethics Committee No. 638/11; CONEP No. 16907
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Total DNA was extracted from 15 stool samples with FastDNA SPIN Kit. Purified libraries were sequenced on a HiSeq 2500 sequencer producing ∼219 million reads, with an average of ∼14 million reads per sample.
uncurated_metadata.section: Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection, DNA Extraction Library Preparation Sequencing
uncurated_metadata.notes: Metadata includes study design, methodology, population characteristics, and ethical approvals.

host_species.evidence_quote: Here, based on shotgun metagenomic data, we characterized the gut microbiome of the Yanomami from Brazil
host_species.notes: Host species inferred from study focus on human (Yanomami and United States) gut microbiome; the Yanomami are human indigenous groups.
